# Nova UI: full documentation for AI agents

Generated by scripts/build-llms.mjs. Do not edit. Source files are listed at the top of each section.
Component names, props, events and methods must match packages/core/dist-docs/API.md.



==== SOURCE: AGENTS.md ====

# AGENTS.md

Instructions for AI coding agents working with or inside the Nova UI repository.

## What this repository is

Nova UI is a design system: web components (Stencil) with generated wrappers for React, Angular and Vue, a CSS library, a Tailwind preset, and an optional rich text editor. Monorepo managed with pnpm.

## Read these first

1. `docs/agents/conventions.md`: which component to use, and the rules that prevent most mistakes.
2. `docs/users/features/README.md`: the feature guides.
3. `packages/core/dist-docs/API.md`: every component, prop, event, method and slot. Treat it as authoritative for names.
4. `docs/humans/architecture.md`: where code lives and what is generated.

A single-file version of the user and agent docs is at `docs/llms-full.txt`. The index is `llms.txt`.

## Using Nova in an application

- Import the stylesheet once: `@import '@omni/css/nova.css';`.
- Use the wrapper for the framework: `@omni/react`, `@omni/angular`, `@omni/vue`, or the plain `ui-*` tags.
- Pass arrays and objects as properties, never as attributes.
- Listen to `ui`-prefixed events and read `event.detail`.
- Give every control a `label` or accessible name.
- Use CSS variables (`--nova-*`) for colour and spacing.
- Sanitise any HTML you didn't write, with `ui-html` or `sanitizeHTML`.

## Working inside this repository

- **Run the checks** before reporting success: `pnpm build`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm check:names`, `pnpm docs:check`. If you can't run one, say so.
- **Don't edit generated files.** `packages/core/dist-docs/*`, `packages/vue/src/components.ts`, `packages/react/src/components/stencil-generated/*`, `packages/angular/src/lib/stencil-generated/*`, `packages/css/src/generated/utilities.css`, `docs/llms-full.txt`. Change the generator's source, then regenerate.
- **Put logic in `packages/core/src/utils`** when it's pure, and test it in `packages/core/test`. Components call the logic.
- **Add strings to `packages/core/src/i18n/messages.ts`** and call `t('key')`. Don't hard-code visible text in components.
- **Use `--nova-*` tokens**, not literal colours or sizes, in component CSS.
- **Props that the component sets itself must be `mutable`.** Stencil warns otherwise.
- **Prop names must not shadow DOM members.** `pnpm check:names` checks this.
- **Local variables named `t` shadow the translator** in files that call `t()`. Use another name.
- **Keep components framework-free.** Core must not import React, Angular or Vue.
- **Document what you add.** Update the feature guide and run `pnpm docs` to refresh the reference.

## Known limits (do not claim otherwise)

- Stencil has not compiled this code in the environment used to write it. Say so if you're asked whether it builds.
- Component interaction is mostly tested through logic, not in a browser. Say which layer your evidence covers.
- Server rendering is not enabled.
- The Vue and Angular wrappers have not been run inside their frameworks in CI.
- Icons are hand-drawn; they render but haven't been checked against a design source.

See `docs/humans/status.md` for the full picture.

## Reporting

When you finish a task, list: what changed, which checks you ran and their results, and which checks you could not run. Don't present unverified output as verified.


==== SOURCE: docs/agents/conventions.md ====

# Conventions for AI agents

Read this before generating code that uses Nova UI. It states the rules that matter and the choices that agents most often get wrong. Also read [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) at the repository root.

## Choose the component

| If you need… | Use | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single-line text | `ui-input` | a bare `<input>` |
| Multi-line text | `ui-textarea` | a bare `<textarea>` |
| Pick one from a list | `ui-select` (searchable) or `ui-radio-group` (few options) | a native `<select>` for long lists |
| Yes or no | `ui-switch` (immediate effect) or `ui-checkbox` (part of a form) | a button |
| A date | `ui-date-picker` | `<input type="date">` when you need Nova styling or range |
| A date range | `ui-date-range-picker` | two date inputs |
| A time | `ui-time-picker` | `<input type="time">` when you need Nova styling |
| A confirmation | `await confirm({...})` | `window.confirm` |
| A short input prompt | `await prompt({...})` | `window.prompt` |
| A notification | `toast.success/error/info/warning` | `alert()` |
| A popup form or detail | `ui-modal` | a custom div |
| Actions on an item | `ui-dropdown` with `ui-menu-item` | a custom menu |
| Tabs | `ui-tabs` with `ui-tab` and `ui-tab-panel` | buttons toggling divs |
| Collapsible content | `ui-accordion` or `ui-collapse` | `<details>` when you need Nova styling or animation |
| A data grid | `ui-table` | a hand-built table with sorting |
| Thousands of rows | `ui-table` with `virtual`, or `ui-virtual-list` | a plain long list |
| A chart | `ui-chart` | an image or a hand-drawn SVG without a data table |
| A small trend | `ui-sparkline` | a chart with axes |
| Reorderable list | `ui-sortable` | custom drag code |
| Board of cards | `ui-kanban` | custom drag code |
| Calendar events | `ui-scheduler` | a custom grid |
| Upload files | `ui-file-upload` | a bare `<input type="file">` for multiple files with validation |
| Rich text | `ui-editor` (import from the editor package) | contenteditable |
| Display HTML from elsewhere | `ui-html` | `innerHTML` |
| Layout | `nova-container`, `nova-stack`, `nova-cluster`, `nova-grid-auto` | custom flex or grid for common patterns |
| A brand palette | `generateTheme` | hand-picked colours that may fail contrast |

## Rules

1. **Import once.** `@import '@omni/css/nova.css'` once per app. Import framework wrappers from the framework package.
2. **Arrays and objects are properties.** Set `options`, `columns`, `rows`, `series`, `labels`, `nodes`, `commands`, `items`, `cards`, `layout`, `events`, `tiers`, `swatches`, `validate`, `uploadFn`, `renderRow`, `toolbar`, `mentionProvider`, `uploadHandler` as JavaScript values. Never as HTML attributes.
3. **Use the event `detail`.** The new value is in `event.detail`. In React: `onUiChange={(e) => set(e.detail)}`. In Angular: `(uiChange)="set($event.detail)"`. In Vue: `@ui-change="(e) => set(e.detail)"`.
4. **Every control has a name.** `label` on inputs and selects, `label` on icon-only buttons, `label` on charts and tables with a `caption`.
5. **Forms use `name`.** Controls submit with their `name` inside `<form>`. Don't wire up hidden inputs yourself.
6. **Don't mutate props.** Keep state in your framework and update it from events.
7. **Use tokens, not hex.** `var(--nova-color-accent)`, not `#0b7a6c`. Tailwind: `bg-nova-accent`.
8. **Sanitise HTML.** Use `<ui-html>` or `sanitizeHTML()`. Never `innerHTML` with untrusted input.
9. **Respect motion.** Don't add animations that the user can't turn off. Components already do this.
10. **Don't edit generated files.** See the table in [Architecture](../humans/architecture.md).
11. **Don't invent props.** Check the [component reference](../../packages/core/dist-docs/API.md) or `custom-elements.json`. If a prop isn't listed, it doesn't exist.

## Framework imports

| Framework | Components | Editor | Helpers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| React | `import { UiButton } from '@omni/react'` | `import { UiEditor } from '@omni/react/editor'` | `import { toast, confirm } from '@omni/react'` |
| Next.js | as React, in a `'use client'` file | as React, with `dynamic(..., { ssr: false })` | as React |
| Angular | `import { UiButton } from '@omni/angular'` (standalone) | `import { UiEditor } from '@omni/angular/editor'` | `import { ThemeService, toast } from '@omni/angular'` |
| Vue 3 | `import { UiButton } from '@omni/vue'` | not yet provided | not yet provided |
| Plain HTML | `<ui-button>` after `defineCustomElements()` | `import '@omni/editor'` | `import { toast } from '@omni/core'` |

## Common mistakes

- `<ui-select options='[...]'>`: wrong. Set `select.options = [...]`.
- `onChange` on a Nova component in React: use `onUiChange`.
- `(change)` in Angular: use `(uiChange)`.
- `ui-datepicker`: the tag is `ui-date-picker`.
- `ui-icon name="warning-circle"`: not in the registry. Use `alert-circle`, `alert-triangle` or `info`. Run `listIcons()` for the list.
- Calling `getHTML()` on the editor: the method is `getContentHTML()`.
- Using `prefix` or `suffix` on `ui-counter`: they're `prefix-text` and `suffix-text`.
- Assuming `ui-table` sorts server data: set `manual` and handle `ui-query-change`.
- Claiming a feature is tested in a browser: only the CSS layer and the logic have browser or unit tests. See [status](../humans/status.md).

## When unsure

Read the component's entry in the reference, then the matching feature guide in `docs/users/features/`. If the docs and the code disagree, the code is right; report the docs bug.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/concepts.md ====

# Concepts

These are the ideas behind the library. Knowing them prevents most problems.

## Web components underneath

Every component is a standard web component (`<ui-*>` custom element). It works without a framework, and each framework gets a thin wrapper that maps props, events and slots onto it. So the same component looks and behaves the same in React, Angular, Vue and plain HTML.

## Props, attributes and events

- **Attributes** are strings in HTML: `size="sm"`, `disabled`.
- **Props** are typed values in frameworks: `size="sm"`, `disabled={true}`, `options={[...]}`. Booleans are real booleans in frameworks.
- **Events** use the `ui` prefix and carry their payload in `detail`. `uiChange` fires when the value changes; `uiInput` fires on every keystroke or drag.

Objects and arrays (`options`, `columns`, `rows`, `series`) are passed as properties, not attributes. Frameworks do this for you. In plain HTML, set them on the element with JavaScript: `el.options = [...]`.

## Slots

Components accept content through named slots. `<ui-button>` takes `slot="start"` and `slot="end"` icons; `<ui-table>` takes `slot="cell:<rowKey>:<columnKey>"` for custom cells. Slots are listed for each component in the reference.

## Forms

Form controls (`ui-input`, `ui-select`, `ui-checkbox`, `ui-date-picker`, and so on) take part in native forms. They submit with their `name`, report `required` through the browser's own validation, and reset with the form. You don't need a custom form library.

## Theme tokens are the source of truth

Colours, spacing, radius, shadows and motion timings are CSS custom properties named `--nova-*`. Components read them, so changing one token changes the whole product, including dark mode. Override tokens; don't fork components. See [Theming](features/theming.md).

## Accessibility is built in, but you still choose labels

Components set roles, states and keyboard handling for you. You provide the text: a `label` on an input, an accessible name on an icon-only button (`label="Delete"`). A component without a name is reported as unlabelled, so always give one.

## Layout is CSS, not components

Use layout classes from `@omni/css` (`nova-container`, `nova-stack`, `nova-grid-auto`) to arrange components. Components are never responsible for page layout. See [Layout and CSS](features/layout-and-css.md).

## Optional packages stay optional

The rich text editor is a separate package because it pulls in Tiptap. Import it only where you use it. The same applies to Tailwind and Vue.

## Translations

Visible text inside components comes from a message catalogue with English defaults. Override any string with `setMessages({...})` before rendering. See [Internationalisation](features/i18n.md).

## Rules that prevent most bugs

1. **Import the stylesheet once.** Without it, components render unstyled.
2. **Give every control a name.** `label`, `aria-label` or visible text.
3. **Set `mutable` values through events.** Don't mutate a component's props directly; listen to its event and update your state.
4. **Sanitise untrusted HTML** with `<ui-html>` or `sanitizeHTML()`, never by setting `innerHTML` yourself.
5. **Use the editor's output as HTML** only after sanitising it on the server.

==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/accessibility.md ====

# Accessibility

Nova targets WCAG 2.2 AA. Components handle roles, states, focus and keyboard use. You supply the names and the content.

## What the components do for you

- Keyboard operation for every interactive component (arrow keys for lists, tabs, menus, grids, sliders, ratings; Enter and Space to activate; Escape to dismiss).
- Visible focus indicators, drawn with outlines that also show in Windows High Contrast mode.
- Roles and states: `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`, `aria-current`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby` linked to hints and errors.
- Focus management: modals trap focus and return it; menus move focus to the first item; toasts announce politely and errors assertively.
- Reduced motion: transitions and continuous animations stop or shorten.
- Touch targets of at least 44px on touch screens.
- Text colours and control borders meet contrast minimums in light and dark themes (checked on every build).

## What you must do

1. **Name everything.** Each input needs a `label` (or `hide-label` for visually hidden text). Each icon-only button needs a `label`.
2. **Use real structure.** One `<h1>` per page, headings in order, landmarks (`<main>`, `<nav>`) around content. Add `nova-skip-link` as the first focusable element.
3. **Describe charts.** Give each chart a meaningful `label`; the component adds the summary and data table.
4. **Don't rely on colour alone.** Pair status with text or an icon (`ui-badge` with `tone` and text).
5. **Keep focus visible.** Don't remove outlines on Nova elements.
6. **Test with the keyboard** from start to finish of every flow, and with a screen reader on at least one.

## Zoom and reflow

Layouts work at 320 CSS pixels wide and at 400 percent zoom with no sideways scrolling, except tables and code. Never disable zoom in the viewport meta tag.

## Known gaps

- Drag-and-drop lists and boards have keyboard alternatives, but the drag itself isn't announced to screen readers. Test with your audience.
- The rich text editor's suggestion popup is not yet announced as a linked combobox.
- Forced-colours (Windows High Contrast) styling is in place but hasn't been tested on Windows yet.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/charts.md ====

# Charts

Charts are drawn in SVG. Each one has a text summary and a data table for screen-reader users, so the numbers are never only visual.

## Line, area, bar and donut

```html
<ui-chart type="line" label="Signups"></ui-chart>
```

Arrays and objects (`labels`, `series`) are properties, so set them in code, never as attributes:

```js
chart.type = 'line';
chart.labels = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar'];
chart.series = [{ name: 'Signups', values: [12, 18, 15] }];
```

A richer example:

```js
chart.type = 'area';
chart.labels = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr'];
chart.series = [
  { name: 'Revenue', values: [12, 18, 15, 22] },
  { name: 'Target', values: [14, 14, 14, 14], color: 'var(--nova-color-fg-muted)' },
];
```

| `type` | Shows | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `line` | One or more series as lines | Points carry tooltips |
| `area` | Lines with a filled area | Good for totals |
| `bar` | Grouped bars | Zero baseline; negatives hang below |
| `donut` | Shares of a whole | Uses the first series; labels name the slices |

Options: `height`, `axes` (gridlines and values), `show-table` (opens the data table), `compact` (1.2k, 3.4M).

Colours come from theme tokens. A series can set its own `color`.

## Sparkline

```html
<ui-sparkline label="Revenue, last 8 weeks" area></ui-sparkline>
```

```js
sparkline.values = [12, 18, 15, 22, 27, 25, 31, 38];
```

Sparklines are small trend lines for tables and cards. The label should say the direction and the period, because the line alone is ambiguous. The description reads "trending up", "down" or "flat".

## Maths helpers

`linearScale`, `niceTicks`, `extent`, `compact`, `linePath`, `areaPath`, `bars` and `donutSlices` are exported from `@omni/core`. Use them when you draw your own SVG and want the same scales.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/colour.md ====

# Colour

## Colour picker

```html
<ui-color-picker name="brand" label="Brand colour" value="#0b7a6c"></ui-color-picker>
<ui-color-picker inline value="#3b82f6"></ui-color-picker>
```

Custom swatches are a property: `picker.swatches = ['#ef4444', '#22c55e', '#3b82f6'];`

```html
```

- Value is a hex string: `#rrggbb`.
- Saturation and brightness are chosen on an area; hue on a slider. Keyboard arrows adjust the area, Shift makes bigger steps.
- Type a hex value, pick a swatch, or use the eyedropper where the browser supports it.
- Events: `ui-input` while dragging, `ui-change` when committed.

## Contrast

Check a colour before you use it for text:

```ts
import { contrastRatio } from '@omni/core';
contrastRatio('#ffffff', '#0b7a6c'); // ≥ 4.5 passes WCAG AA for body text
```

For a whole brand palette, use the theme generator in [Theming](theming.md). It guarantees AA contrast for text on accent colours.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/data-tables.md ====

# Data tables

`<ui-table>` shows rows with sorting, search, selection, pagination, export, resizing, expandable rows and virtual scrolling.

## Basic table

```html
<ui-table caption="Team" searchable selectable paginate></ui-table>
```

Set data with properties:

```js
table.columns = [
  { key: 'name', label: 'Name', sortable: true },
  { key: 'spend', label: 'Spend', align: 'end', sortable: true, format: (v) => `$${v.toLocaleString()}` },
];
table.rows = [{ id: 1, name: 'Ada', spend: 4200 }];
```

- `row-key` names the id field (default `id`). Selection and custom cells use it.
- `columns`: `key`, `label`, `sortable`, `align`, `width`, `format`.
- Clicking a sortable header cycles ascending, descending, off.

## Browser or server data

- **Browser mode** (default): pass every row. Search, sort and paging happen in the table.
- **Server mode**: set `manual`, pass the current page as `rows` and the full count as `total`. Handle `ui-query-change`, which carries `{ page, pageSize, sort, search }`. Search is debounced.

```tsx
<UiTable
  manual
  rows={rows}
  total={total}
  page={query.page}
  pageSize={query.pageSize}
  onUiQueryChange={(e) => setQuery(e.detail)}
/>
```

## Selection

`selectable` adds checkboxes and a select-all for the page. Selection survives page changes and is reported in `ui-selection-change`. Put actions for selected rows in `slot="bulk-actions"`.

## Custom cells

```html
<ui-table>
  <ui-badge slot="cell:u1:status" tone="success">Active</ui-badge>
</ui-table>
```

Use the slot name `cell:<rowKey>:<columnKey>`. Any markup works there.

## Expandable rows and resizing

- `expandable` adds a toggle column. Put detail content in `slot="expand:<rowKey>"`.
- `resizable` lets users drag header edges to change column widths.

## Export

`exportable` adds an Export CSV button. It exports every row that matches the current search and sort, not just the visible page. You can also call it yourself:

```js
const csv = await table.exportCSV();
```

Exported cells beginning with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` are neutralised so spreadsheets don't run them as formulas.

## Virtual scrolling

For thousands of rows:

```html
<ui-table virtual max-height="420px" row-height="44" paginate="false"></ui-table>
```

Virtual mode needs `max-height` (the scroll area) and a fixed `row-height`. It doesn't work with expandable rows. Only rows on screen are rendered.

## Tree, virtual list

- `<ui-tree>` shows a hierarchy with expand and collapse, single selection and full keyboard support. Pass `nodes` as `{ id, label, icon?, children? }`.
- `<ui-virtual-list>` renders long lists with a `count`, a `row-height` and a `render-row` function.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/dates.md ====

# Dates and times

Dates are plain `YYYY-MM-DD` strings, so time zones never shift them. Times are `HH:mm` (24-hour).

## Single date

```html
<ui-date-picker name="start" label="Start date" min="2026-01-01" max="2027-12-31" clearable></ui-date-picker>
```

- Type a date or pick one from the calendar.
- `min` and `max` disable days outside the range.
- Event: `ui-change` with the new `YYYY-MM-DD` string (or `""` when cleared).

## Date range

```html
<ui-date-range-picker name="period" label="Report period" presets></ui-date-range-picker>
```

- Click a start day, then an end day. Order is fixed for you, so a backwards second click still works.
- `presets` adds Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month and This year.
- `value` is `{ start, end }`; event `ui-change` gives the same shape. Use the `today` prop in tests and server-rendered pages.

## Calendar only

`<ui-calendar>` is the month grid on its own, for inline selection. Arrow keys move by day and week, PageUp and PageDown change month, Shift with PageUp or PageDown changes year.

## Time

```html
<ui-time-picker name="start" label="Start" min="08:00" max="18:00" step="15"></ui-time-picker>
```

- Accepts `930`, `9:30` or `09:30`. Invalid or out-of-range entries show an error.
- The list suggests slots at `step` minutes.

## Helpers

The date and time maths is exported for your own code: `parseISO`, `toISO`, `addDays`, `addMonths`, `monthGrid`, `parseTime`, `durationMinutes`, `timeSlots`. Use these rather than `new Date('2026-03-01')`, which parses in UTC and can show the wrong day.

## Scheduling

Events on a calendar with month and week views are in [Lists, boards and scheduling](lists-boards-scheduling.md).


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/editor.md ====

# Rich text editor

`<ui-editor>` is a rich text editor built on Tiptap, with a toolbar made from Nova buttons, menus and icons. It's a separate package so it only loads where you use it.

```bash
pnpm add @omni/editor
```

```tsx
// React
import { UiEditor } from '@omni/react/editor';

<UiEditor
  label="Description"
  preset="standard"
  value={html}
  onUiChange={(e) => setHtml(e.detail)}
  uploadHandler={async (file) => (await storage.upload(file)).url}
/>
```

Angular: `import { UiEditor } from '@omni/angular/editor'`. HTML: `import '@omni/editor'`, then `<ui-editor preset="standard"></ui-editor>`.

## Toolbar

- `preset`: `minimal`, `standard` or `full`.
- `toolbar`: your own list, in order. `'|'` is a separator.

Available items: `undo redo heading bold italic underline strike code textColor highlight alignLeft alignCenter alignRight bulletList orderedList taskList blockquote codeBlock hr link image attachment table`.

Keyboard shortcuts follow the usual ones: Ctrl or Cmd with B, I, U, Z; Ctrl or Cmd with K for a link.

## Commands and mentions

- `slashCommands` (default on): typing `/` opens a menu of blocks your toolbar allows.
- `mentionProvider(query)` turns on `@` mentions. Return `{ id, label, description? }[]`, synchronously or as a promise.

## Uploads

- `uploadHandler(file)` resolves with a URL, or `{ url, alt }`. It's used for pasted, dropped and chosen files.
- `accept` (images, default `image/*`), `attachmentAccept` (other files), `maxFileSize` in bytes.
- Without `uploadHandler`, images are embedded as data URLs and attachments are refused with a message.

## Limits and state

- `maxLength` shows a live counter and enforces the limit.
- `readonly`, `disabled`, `required`, `name` (submits the HTML with a form).
- `minHeight`, `maxHeight`: the writing area scrolls past `maxHeight`.

## Methods

`getContentHTML()`, `getContentJSON()`, `getContentText()`, `setContent(html)`, `insertContent(html)`, `clear()`, `focusEditor()`, and `getEditor()` for the underlying Tiptap editor.

## Events

`ui-change` (HTML), `ui-focus`, `ui-blur`, `ui-ready`, `ui-upload-start`, `ui-upload-complete`, `ui-upload-error`.

## Security: sanitise the HTML

The editor's value is HTML. The editor blocks script-capable links and image sources, but you must still sanitise HTML before storing it server-side or rendering it elsewhere. On the client, render it with `<ui-html>`, which sanitises it for you.

## Notes

- The editor renders in light DOM so the browser's text selection, spellcheck and input methods work normally. Its CSS is prefixed `nova-ed`, so it can't leak into your page.
- Pinned to Tiptap v2.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/feedback.md ====

# Feedback and status

Components that show state: whether something is happening, whether it worked, and what the numbers are.

## Alerts

```html
<ui-alert tone="success" heading="Saved">Your changes are live.</ui-alert>
<ui-alert tone="danger" heading="Could not save" dismissible>Check your connection and try again.</ui-alert>
```

- `tone`: `info`, `success`, `warning` or `danger`. Danger and warning are announced assertively; the others politely.
- `dismissible` adds a close button. Event: `ui-dismiss`.
- Pair the tone with the text. Colour alone isn't enough.

## Badges

```html
<ui-badge tone="success" dot>Active</ui-badge>
<ui-badge tone="warning" variant="outline">Pending</ui-badge>
<ui-badge tone="danger" variant="solid">Failed</ui-badge>
```

Tones: `neutral`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`. Variants: `soft` (default), `solid`, `outline`.

## Avatars

```html
<ui-avatar name="Ada Lovelace"></ui-avatar>
<ui-avatar src="/people/ada.jpg" name="Ada Lovelace" shape="square" size="lg"></ui-avatar>
```

Shows initials when there's no image or the image fails to load. `name` is the accessible name.

## Loading states

```html
<ui-spinner label="Saving"></ui-spinner>
<ui-progress label="Upload" value="64" show-value></ui-progress>
<ui-progress label="Processing"></ui-progress>
<ui-skeleton lines="3"></ui-skeleton>
```

- Spinner: `label` is announced. Use it for short waits.
- Progress: pass `value`. Leave it unset for an indeterminate bar when you don't know the total.
- Skeleton: placeholder shapes while content loads. Mark the loading region with `aria-busy="true"` on its container.

## Counters

```html
<ui-counter value="12840" locale="en-US"></ui-counter>
<ui-counter value="99.9" decimals="1" suffix-text="%"></ui-counter>
```

Counts up when it becomes visible. Users who prefer reduced motion see the final number straight away.

## Cards

```html
<ui-card variant="raised">
  <span slot="header">Profile</span>
  <p>Card body.</p>
  <div slot="footer">…</div>
</ui-card>
```

- `variant`: `outlined` (default), `raised` or `flat`.
- `interactive` adds hover and focus states. Wrap the card in a link or button for the actual action.

## Dialogs and notifications

For confirmations, prompts and toasts see [Overlays](overlays.md).


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/file-upload.md ====

# File upload

`<ui-file-upload>` is a dropzone with a file list. It validates files before anything is uploaded and reports every problem at once.

```html
<ui-file-upload label="Attachments" accept=".pdf,.png,.jpg" max-size="5242880" max-files="4"></ui-file-upload>
```

## Validation

- `accept`: allowed extensions or MIME types, for example `image/*,.pdf`.
- `max-size`: largest single file, in bytes.
- `max-files`: how many files may be selected in total.
- `max-total-size`: all files together, in bytes.

Rejected files are listed with the reason, for example "`report.exe` isn't an allowed file type."

## Uploading

Pass an upload function. Each file uploads as it's added, with progress:

```js
upload.uploadFn = (file, onProgress) =>
  uploadToStorage(file, { onProgress: (p) => onProgress(p) }); // resolves with the URL
```

- Events: `ui-files` (accepted files), `ui-uploaded` (`{ file, url }`), `ui-rejected` (problems), `ui-remove`.
- Without `uploadFn`, you receive files through `ui-files` and handle them yourself.
- `name` submits the uploaded URLs with the form.

## Clear

```js
await upload.clear();
```

## Rich text editor uploads

The editor has its own upload path (paste, drop and insert). See [Rich text editor](editor.md).


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/forms.md ====

# Forms

Form controls submit with a surrounding `<form>`, report `required` through the browser, and reset with the form. Give every control a `name`.

## Text

```html
<ui-input name="email" type="email" label="Email" hint="We never share it" required></ui-input>
<ui-input name="code" label="Code" error="Enter the full code"></ui-input>
<ui-textarea name="bio" label="Bio" maxlength="160" autoresize></ui-textarea>
```

- `label` is required for accessibility. Use `hide-label` to keep it for screen readers only.
- `hint` explains; `error` replaces the hint and marks the field invalid.
- Events: `ui-input` on every keystroke, `ui-change` when the value is committed.
- `ui-input` accepts `prefix` and `suffix` slots for icons.

## Choices

```html
<ui-checkbox name="terms" required>I agree</ui-checkbox>
<ui-switch name="digest" checked>Weekly digest</ui-switch>

<ui-radio-group name="plan" label="Plan" value="team">
  <ui-radio value="solo">Solo</ui-radio>
  <ui-radio value="team">Team</ui-radio>
  <ui-radio value="org" disabled>Organisation</ui-radio>
</ui-radio-group>
```

- `ui-radio-group` handles arrow keys and selection; the group is the form control.
- A checkbox with no visible text needs `label` for its accessible name.

## Ranges and ratings

```html
<ui-slider name="volume" label="Volume" min="0" max="100" step="5" show-value></ui-slider>
<ui-rating name="score" max="5" label="Rate this"></ui-rating>
```

## Codes and tags

```html
<ui-otp-input name="otp" length="6" label="Verification code"></ui-otp-input>
<ui-tag-input name="emails" label="Invite"></ui-tag-input>
```

- `ui-otp-input` auto-advances, accepts paste, and supports SMS autofill. Set `type="alphanumeric"` if needed.
- `ui-tag-input` accepts Enter, comma or paste. Set a `validate` function (a property) that returns `true` or an error string; rejected tags fire `ui-reject`.

```js
tags.validate = (tag) => /^\S+@\S+\.\S+$/.test(tag) || 'Enter a valid email.';
```

## Your own control: `ui-field`

Wrap any control that has no label of its own, to get a label, hint, error and `aria-describedby`:

```html
<ui-field label="Region" hint="Used for billing">
  <select name="region"><option>UK</option><option>India</option></select>
</ui-field>
```

## Validation

Required fields use the browser's validation. For custom rules, check your own values and pass an `error` string back into the component.

```tsx
<UiInput name="email" label="Email" error={email && !email.includes('@') ? 'Enter a valid email' : undefined} />
```

## Submitting

```ts
form.addEventListener('submit', (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  const data = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form));
});
```


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/i18n.md ====

# Internationalisation

Visible text inside components (labels, placeholders, aria-labels, messages) comes from one catalogue with English defaults. Override any of it.

```ts
import { setMessages, DEFAULT_MESSAGES } from '@omni/core';

setMessages({
  close: 'Fermer',
  noResults: 'Aucun résultat',
  showingRange: 'Affichage de {from} à {to} sur {total}',
});
```

Call `setMessages` once before your first render. Values can contain `{placeholders}`, which components fill in. Keys you don't set stay in English.

## Finding keys

`DEFAULT_MESSAGES` lists every key with its English text. The type `MessageKey` is the union of those keys, so your editor autocompletes them.

## Locale-aware formatting

Dates, numbers and times use the browser's `Intl` APIs. Pass `locale` to a component to override the browser default:

```html
<ui-date-picker locale="fr-FR" name="start"></ui-date-picker>
<ui-counter value="12840" locale="de-DE"></ui-counter>
```

## Right-to-left

Components and layout classes use logical properties, so `<html dir="rtl">` flips layout, padding, borders and alignment. Icons that imply a direction (arrows, chevrons) need flipping in your own CSS.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/icons.md ====

# Icons

`<ui-icon>` draws icons from one of two sets:

- **Nova** (default): about 70 built-in line icons drawn as SVG. No font needed.
- **Material**: Google's [Material Symbols](https://fonts.google.com/icons), drawn with the Material font. Nova names are mapped to Material names automatically, so every component works in either set.

## Load the Material font (once)

Add this to your page's `<head>`. It's the same font your app loads from Google Fonts:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Material+Symbols+Outlined:opsz,wght,FILL,GRAD@20..48,100..700,0..1,-50..200&display=block" />
```

Skip this if you use only the Nova set.

## Offline: bundled Material icons

Instead of the Google link, `@omni/css` can ship the Material Symbols font itself. A maintainer runs this once, and rebuilds:

```bash
pnpm --filter @omni/css icons:update
pnpm --filter @omni/css build
```

Then load the generated stylesheet and use the `nova-icon` classes (no network needed):

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@omni/css/icons.css" />
<span class="nova-icon nova-icon-home" aria-hidden="true"></span>
<span class="nova-icon nova-icon-star nova-icon-filled nova-icon-lg"></span>
```

Sizes: `nova-icon-xs`, `-sm`, `-md`, `-lg`, `-xl`. The icon names are listed in `@omni/css/material-icon-names.json`. The official licence is copied alongside the font.

## Choose the set

```js
import { setIconLibrary } from '@omni/core';

setIconLibrary('material'); // every <ui-icon> on the page switches; icons redraw automatically
setIconLibrary('nova');
```

A single icon can override the page setting:

```html
<ui-icon name="check" library="material"></ui-icon>
<ui-icon name="check" library="nova"></ui-icon>
```

Read the current setting with `getIconLibrary()`. Listen for changes with `onIconLibraryChange(fn)`.

## Use icons

```html
<ui-icon name="check"></ui-icon>
<ui-icon name="chevron-down" size="1.25rem"></ui-icon>
<ui-icon name="alert-circle" label="Warning"></ui-icon>
<ui-button icon-only label="Delete"><ui-icon name="trash"></ui-icon></ui-button>
```

- Icons scale with the text around them unless you set `size`.
- With no `label` the icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers. Set a `label` when the icon carries meaning on its own.
- `filled` fills the shape, for example a solid star or a filled Material icon.

## Names

In the Material set, Nova names map to Material names. Some common ones:

| Nova name | Material name | Nova name | Material name |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `check` | `check` | `trash` | `delete` |
| `x` | `close` | `user` | `person` |
| `search` | `search` | `bell` | `notifications` |
| `chevron-down` | `expand_more` | `settings` | `settings` |
| `plus` | `add` | `calendar` | `calendar_month` |
| `upload` | `upload` | `download` | `download` |

Use a Material name directly if it isn't in the table. It's looked up as a Material ligature. Run `MATERIAL_NAMES` from `@omni/core` for the complete mapping.

## Add your own

```js
import { registerIcons } from '@omni/core';

registerIcons({
  logo: '<path d="M4 4h16v16H4z"/>', // inner SVG, 24 x 24 viewBox, stroked
});
```

A registered icon keeps its own drawing in either set, unless its name is also in the Material mapping.

## Notes

- Icons take the colour of the text around them (`currentColor`).
- In the Material set, text in the Material font is shown as plain text if the font hasn't loaded. Load the font, or use `display=block` as shown above.
- In plain CSS you can use the Material font directly: `<span class="material-symbols-outlined">home</span>`, once the font is loaded.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/layout-and-css.md ====

# Layout and CSS

`@omni/css` provides layout primitives, responsive utilities, container queries, typography and CSS-only components. It's useful with or without the web components.

The complete guide, with breakpoints, a decision table ("which layout tool do I use?"), recipes and accessibility notes, is in **[packages/css/GUIDELINES.md](../../../packages/css/GUIDELINES.md)**. A live, resizable version is at `packages/css/docs/index.html`.

## The essentials

```html
<div class="nova-container nova-section nova-stack">
  <h1 class="nova-h2">Dashboard</h1>
  <div class="nova-grid-auto nova-grid-auto-md nova-gap-4">…</div>
  <div class="nova-cluster nova-cluster-between">…</div>
</div>
```

| Need | Class |
| --- | --- |
| Centred content with safe margins | `nova-container` (sizes: `-sm`, `-md`, `-lg`, `-prose`) |
| Vertical spacing | `nova-stack` (`nova-stack-sm`, `-lg`) |
| Wrapping row | `nova-cluster` |
| Cards that fill the space | `nova-grid-auto` (`nova-grid-auto-sm`, `-md`, `-lg`) |
| Fixed side and fluid main | `nova-sidebar` |
| Row that stacks below a width | `nova-switcher` |
| App frame | `nova-shell`, `nova-shell-sidebar`, `nova-shell-aside` |

## Responsive without thinking

Classes are mobile first. `nova-md-cols-3` means "three columns from 768px up". Visibility works the same way: `nova-hide-below-md`, `nova-hide-md-up`.

## Container queries

`nova-cq` on a parent makes its children respond to its width, not the screen: `nova-cq-md-cols-2`.

## Themes

Every colour in these classes is a token, so `nova-bg-surface` and `nova-text-muted` follow light and dark mode.

## Motion helpers

`nova-scroll-reveal` and `nova-scroll-progress` animate with the browser's scroll timeline. They are inert where unsupported, and disabled for reduced motion.

## Tailwind

If you use Tailwind, add the [preset](../frameworks/tailwind.md). Nova's layout classes and Tailwind's can sit side by side.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/lists-boards-scheduling.md ====

# Lists, boards and scheduling

## Sortable list

```js
sortable.items = [{ id: 'a', label: 'Design' }, { id: 'b', label: 'Build' }];
sortable.addEventListener('ui-reorder', (e) => save(e.detail));
```

- Drag with a pointer, or focus an item and press Alt with the up or down arrow.
- The keyboard path is the one to test. It's the same for screen-reader users.

## Kanban board

```js
board.columns = [{ id: 'todo', title: 'To do' }, { id: 'doing', title: 'In progress' }, { id: 'done', title: 'Done' }];
board.cards = [{ id: '1', title: 'Write docs', detail: 'Owner: Ada' }];
board.layout = { todo: ['1'], doing: [], done: [] };
board.addEventListener('ui-move', (e) => save(e.detail.layout));
```

- Drag cards between columns, or focus a card and use Alt with the arrow keys:
  - Alt + Up or Down reorders within a column.
  - Alt + Left or Right moves the card to the neighbouring column.
- `layout` maps each column id to its ordered card ids. Keep it in your state; the board emits every change.

## Scheduler

```js
scheduler.events = [
  { id: 'e1', title: 'Design review', start: '2026-11-16', startTime: '10:00', endTime: '11:00' },
  { id: 'e2', title: 'Conference', start: '2026-11-18', end: '2026-11-20' },
];
scheduler.view = 'week';
scheduler.addEventListener('ui-event-click', (e) => open(e.detail));
```

- `view`: `month` or `week`.
- Events without `startTime` are all-day. Multi-day events show on each day they cover.
- In week view, overlapping timed events sit side by side.
- Use `date` to choose the week or month shown, `first-day-of-week` (0 Sunday, 1 Monday), and `day-start` / `day-end` for the visible hours.
- Each event is a real button, so keyboard and screen-reader users reach every event.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/motion.md ====

# Motion

Motion explains change; it never carries information on its own. Every animation here respects `prefers-reduced-motion`, and users who prefer less motion see the final state immediately.

## Entrance on scroll

```html
<ui-reveal animation="slide-up" duration="500" delay="0" threshold="0.15">
  <p>Appears when scrolled into view.</p>
</ui-reveal>
```

`animation`: `fade`, `slide-up`, `slide-down`, `slide-left`, `slide-right` or `scale`. `repeat` replays each time it re-enters the view. Event: `ui-reveal`.

## Staggered entrance

```html
<ui-stagger animation="slide-up" step="70" trigger="visible">
  <p>First</p><p>Second</p><p>Third</p>
</ui-stagger>
```

`trigger="load"` plays at once; `visible` waits until scrolled into view.

## Counters

```html
<ui-counter value="12840" locale="en-US" duration="1200"></ui-counter>
<ui-counter value="99.9" decimals="1" suffix-text="%"></ui-counter>
```

Counts up when visible. Screen readers hear the final value only.

## Marquee

```html
<ui-marquee speed="40" pause-on-hover>
  <img src="/logo-a.svg" alt="Acme" /><img src="/logo-b.svg" alt="Globex" />
</ui-marquee>
```

An endless ticker. It stops for reduced-motion users.

## Scroll progress

```html
<ui-scroll-progress label="Reading progress"></ui-scroll-progress>
```

A fixed bar that tracks how far the page has scrolled, or a container with `target`.

## Helpers

```ts
import { animateIn, staggerIn, playExit, withViewTransition } from '@omni/core';

await animateIn(el, 'fade', { duration: 300 });
await playExit(el);                          // animate out before removing
await withViewTransition(() => swapPage());  // cross-fade between states
```

- `withViewTransition` uses the browser's View Transitions API where it exists and updates immediately where it doesn't.
- In React, `usePresence(open, ms)` keeps an element mounted while it exits. See [React](../frameworks/react.md).

## Scroll-linked CSS

With `@omni/css`: `nova-scroll-reveal` ties an element's fade and rise to its position in the viewport, and `nova-scroll-progress` scales an element with page scroll. No JavaScript runs.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/navigation.md ====

# Navigation

## Tabs

```html
<ui-tabs label="Project sections" value="overview">
  <ui-tab value="overview">Overview</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab value="activity">Activity</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab value="billing" disabled>Billing</ui-tab>
  <ui-tab-panel value="overview">…</ui-tab-panel>
  <ui-tab-panel value="activity">…</ui-tab-panel>
</ui-tabs>
```

- `variant="pills"` for a segmented look; `orientation="vertical"` for a side list.
- Arrow keys move between tabs. `activation="manual"` waits for Enter or Space.
- Event: `ui-change` with the tab value.

## Accordion

```html
<ui-accordion>
  <ui-accordion-item heading="What is Nova?" open>…</ui-accordion-item>
  <ui-accordion-item heading="Does it work with Angular?">…</ui-accordion-item>
</ui-accordion>
```

Only one item is open at a time unless you set `multiple`.

## Breadcrumb

```html
<ui-breadcrumb max-items="3">
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="/">Home</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item href="/projects">Projects</ui-breadcrumb-item>
  <ui-breadcrumb-item>Nova</ui-breadcrumb-item>
</ui-breadcrumb>
```

The last item is the current page. Long trails fold into an expandable "…".

## Pagination

```html
<ui-pagination page="4" total="240" page-size="10" label="Results"></ui-pagination>
```

Pass `page-count` directly if you know the number of pages. Event: `ui-change` with the new page.

## Stepper

```html
<ui-stepper current="1" clickable>
  <ui-step heading="Account" description="Your details"></ui-step>
  <ui-step heading="Workspace"></ui-step>
  <ui-step heading="Invite"></ui-step>
</ui-stepper>
```

Set `error` on a step to flag a problem. With `clickable`, users can go back to completed steps.

## Site navigation and menubar

```html
<ui-nav-menu label="Site">
  <ui-nav-item label="Home" href="/" current></ui-nav-item>
  <ui-nav-item label="Products">
    <a href="/analytics">Analytics</a>
    <a href="/reports">Reports</a>
  </ui-nav-item>
</ui-nav-menu>

<ui-menubar label="Application">
  <ui-menubar-menu label="File"><ui-menu-item value="new">New</ui-menu-item></ui-menubar-menu>
  <ui-menubar-menu label="Edit"><ui-menu-item value="undo">Undo</ui-menu-item></ui-menubar-menu>
</ui-menubar>
```

Nav items with children open on click, one at a time. In a menubar, once a menu is open, hovering or pressing Left and Right switches menus.

## Sidebar

```html
<ui-sidebar label="Main" storage-key="sidebar">
  <ui-sidebar-item label="Overview" icon="home" current href="/"></ui-sidebar-item>
  <ui-sidebar-item label="Projects" icon="folder" badge="3" href="/projects"></ui-sidebar-item>
  <ui-sidebar-item label="Reports" icon="bar-chart" group open>
    <ui-sidebar-item label="Weekly" href="/weekly"></ui-sidebar-item>
  </ui-sidebar-item>
</ui-sidebar>
```

- `collapsed` shows icons only; labels become tooltips.
- `storage-key` remembers the collapsed state between visits.
- Pair it with `nova-shell-sidebar` from [layout](layout-and-css.md) to build an app frame.

## Split panes

```html
<ui-split ratio="0.3" min-a="160" min-b="240" storage-key="split">
  <div slot="a">List</div>
  <div slot="b">Detail</div>
</ui-split>
```

Drag the divider, or focus it and use arrows (Shift for larger steps), Home or End. Double-click resets to 50 percent. `ratio` is the first pane's share, from 0 to 1.

## Collapse

```html
<ui-collapse peek="Shipping, returns and exchanges">
  <span slot="label">Delivery</span>
  Full details here.
</ui-collapse>
```

Animates its height smoothly. Use it for disclosure of secondary content, not for primary navigation.

## Carousel

```html
<ui-carousel label="Highlights" slides-per-view="2" autoplay="5000">
  <div>Slide one</div>
  <div>Slide two</div>
</ui-carousel>
```

- Swipe, use the arrows, or pick a dot. Keyboard users can use the arrow buttons and focus the track.
- `slides-per-view` shows several slides at once. `loop` wraps around. `autoplay` (milliseconds) advances automatically, pauses on hover or focus, and has a pause button. Autoplay is off for users who prefer reduced motion.
- Event: `ui-change` with the index of the first visible slide.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/overlays.md ====

# Overlays

Overlays float above the page: dialogs, drawers, menus, tooltips and notifications. They handle focus, Escape and outside clicks for you.

## Modal and drawer

```html
<ui-modal open heading="Delete project?" size="sm">
  This removes every file in it.
  <div slot="footer">
    <ui-button variant="ghost">Cancel</ui-button>
    <ui-button variant="danger">Delete</ui-button>
  </div>
</ui-modal>

<ui-drawer open side="right" heading="Filters">…</ui-drawer>
```

- Set `open` to show; the modal emits `ui-close` when dismissed. Keep your state in sync with that event.
- Focus is trapped inside while open, and returns to the trigger on close.
- `size`: `sm`, `md`, `lg` or `full`. Drawers take `side` of `left`, `right`, `top` or `bottom`.
- Set `dismissible="false"` only when the user must choose an action.

## Confirm and prompt

For the common case, skip the modal entirely:

```ts
import { confirm, prompt } from '@omni/core';

if (await confirm({ title: 'Delete project?', message: 'This cannot be undone.', confirmLabel: 'Delete', danger: true })) {
  // delete
}

const name = await prompt({
  title: 'Rename',
  defaultValue: current,
  validate: (v) => (v.length < 3 ? 'Use at least 3 characters.' : undefined),
});
```

Requests queue, so two dialogs never overlap. `confirm` resolves `true` or `false`; `prompt` resolves the text or `null` when cancelled.

## Popover, tooltip

```html
<ui-popover placement="bottom-start" label="Share">
  <ui-button slot="trigger">Share</ui-button>
  <p>Anyone with the link can view.</p>
</ui-popover>

<ui-tooltip content="Saved 2 minutes ago" placement="top">
  <ui-button variant="ghost">Status</ui-button>
</ui-tooltip>
```

Popovers render in the browser's top layer, so `overflow: hidden` parents can't clip them.

## Menus

```html
<ui-dropdown>
  <ui-button slot="trigger">Actions</ui-button>
  <ui-menu-item value="rename">Rename</ui-menu-item>
  <ui-menu-item value="delete" tone="danger" divider>Delete</ui-menu-item>
</ui-dropdown>

<ui-context-menu>
  <div>Right-click me</div>
  <ui-menu-item slot="menu" value="copy">Copy</ui-menu-item>
</ui-context-menu>
```

- Arrow keys, Home and End move; typing jumps to a matching item; Enter chooses; Escape closes.
- The chosen item arrives in `ui-select` as `{ value, label }`.

## Searchable select

```html
<ui-select name="owner" label="Owner" searchable clearable></ui-select>
```

```js
select.options = [{ value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Lovelace' }, { value: 'grace', label: 'Grace Hopper' }];
```

Options are a property, not an attribute.

- Single or `multiple` selection. Multiple shows removable chips.
- Filtering is built in. For server-side search set `filter="false"` and load options on `ui-search`.

## Command palette

```html
<ui-command-palette hotkey="mod+k"></ui-command-palette>
```

Set `commands` to an array of `{ id, label, group, icon, shortcut, keywords }`. `mod` is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Chosen commands fire `ui-select`.

## Notifications

```ts
import { toast } from '@omni/core';

toast.success('Saved');
toast.error({ title: 'Upload failed', description: 'Check your connection.', actionLabel: 'Retry', onAction: retry });
const { id, dismiss } = toast.info('Syncing…', { duration: 0 });
```

Render `<ui-toaster>` once near the root. Toasts pause while hovered and sit above open dialogs.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/page-blocks.md ====

# Page blocks

Blocks are ready-made page compositions built from Nova components and layout classes. They're starting points: copy one into your app and change the content.

```tsx
import { LoginBlock, PricingBlock, SettingsBlock, DashboardBlock, OnboardingBlock } from '@omni/react';
```

| Block | Use it for | Key props |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `LoginBlock` | Sign-in card with email, password and remember-me | `title`, `subtitle`, `onSubmit(email, password)`, `footer` |
| `PricingBlock` | Pricing tiers that stack on phones | `tiers: { name, price, period?, features, featured?, cta? }[]` |
| `SettingsBlock` | Settings with a section sidebar | `sections`, `active`, `children` |
| `DashboardBlock` | KPI cards, a trend chart and a table | `title`, `kpis`, `months`, `series`, `columns`, `rows`, `notice` |
| `OnboardingBlock` | Multi-step setup | `step`, `steps`, `children` |

Blocks are React-only for now. Angular and Vue users can build the same layouts from the components; the [playground](../../../apps/playground-vite/src/BlocksDemo.tsx) shows each block in use.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/safe-html.md ====

# Safe HTML

Use `<ui-html>` whenever you display HTML you don't fully control: comments, CMS content, rich text from users, or the editor's output.

```html
<ui-html prose html="<h3>Notes</h3><p>Fixed <strong>export</strong>.</p>"></ui-html>
```

```js
html.html = untrustedHtml;
html.allowImages = false; // strips <img> elements
```

## What is removed

- `<script>`, `<style>`, `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, forms and form controls, and embedded SVG or MathML, along with their contents.
- Every `on*` event attribute.
- `javascript:`, `vbscript:` and `data:text/html` links and image sources. Only `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `tel` and relative links are kept; images also allow base64 PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and AVIF.
- HTML comments, which can hide conditional markup.
- Unknown tags are unwrapped: their text stays, the tag goes.
- `target="_blank"` links receive `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

## Functions

```ts
import { sanitizeHTML, isSafeLink, isSafeImage } from '@omni/core';
const clean = sanitizeHTML(untrusted);
```

## Limits

This sanitiser covers common cases and is tested against the attacks listed above. For content from the public internet on a high-risk surface, also use a maintained sanitiser such as DOMPurify at your server boundary. Defence in depth is cheap here.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/theming.md ====

# Theming

Nova has a light and a dark theme, and you can change any colour, radius, shadow, font or timing with CSS variables.

## Light, dark and system

```js
import { setThemeMode, getThemeMode, onThemeChange } from '@omni/core';

setThemeMode('dark');         // 'light' | 'dark' | 'system'
onThemeChange((mode, resolved) => console.log(mode, resolved));
```

Or drop in `<ui-theme-toggle>`, a button that cycles light, dark and system. The choice is saved in `localStorage` under `nova-ui-theme` and applied before first paint if you add the theme script (see [Next.js](../frameworks/nextjs.md) and [Vite](../frameworks/vite.md)).

The page gets `data-theme="light"` or `"dark"` on `<html>`. Nova's tokens switch with it.

## Brand colours

Generate a complete palette from one colour. The generator guarantees that text on the accent and the accent on the surface meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) in both themes:

```ts
import { generateTheme, themeToCSS } from '@omni/core';

const theme = generateTheme('#7c3aed');
console.log(theme.warnings);            // [] when every pair passes
document.head.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', `<style>${themeToCSS(theme)}</style>`);
```

Use `theme.light` and `theme.dark` to drive your own tokens.

## Override tokens

```css
:root {
  --nova-color-accent: #5b3fd1;
  --nova-color-accent-hover: #4a32b0;
  --nova-radius-control: 10px;
}
[data-theme='dark'] {
  --nova-color-accent: #a99bff;
}
```

Overrides apply to every component and every framework. Keep them in one stylesheet.

## Token reference

| Group | Examples |
| --- | --- |
| Surfaces | `--nova-color-bg`, `--nova-color-surface`, `--nova-color-surface-raised`, `--nova-color-surface-sunken` |
| Text | `--nova-color-fg`, `--nova-color-fg-muted`, `--nova-color-fg-subtle`, `--nova-color-fg-on-accent` |
| Accent | `--nova-color-accent`, `--nova-color-accent-hover`, `--nova-color-accent-soft` |
| Status | `--nova-color-success`, `--nova-color-warning`, `--nova-color-danger`, `--nova-color-info` (and `-soft`) |
| Shape | `--nova-radius-control`, `--nova-radius-surface`, `--nova-radius-pill` |
| Elevation | `--nova-shadow-sm`, `--nova-shadow-md`, `--nova-shadow-lg`, `--nova-focus-ring` |
| Type | `--nova-font-sans`, `--nova-font-mono`, `--nova-text-xs` to `--nova-text-5xl` |
| Space | `--nova-space-1` to `--nova-space-16`, `--nova-space-fluid-s` to `-xl` |
| Motion | `--nova-duration-fast`, `--nova-duration-base`, `--nova-ease-standard` |

## Translucent tints

Hover, selection, drop-target and scrim colours are translucent, so they sit on whatever the surface is and never hide it. The tokens:

| Token | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `--nova-tint-hover` | Hover backgrounds on rows, buttons, menu items and tabs |
| `--nova-tint-accent` | Selected rows, active sidebar items, selected tree nodes, option highlights |
| `--nova-tint-accent-strong` | Pressed states and drop targets |
| `--nova-tint-danger`, `-success`, `-warning`, `-info` | Status tints for your own panels |
| `--nova-scrim` | Dialog backdrops |

Text is never placed directly on a tint without a check. The build blends each tint onto its surface and tests the text against it, so accent text on a selected row uses `--nova-color-accent-hover`, which keeps AA contrast.

Override a tint to change how strong a state looks:

```css
:root { --nova-tint-accent: rgb(91 63 209 / 0.14); }
[data-theme='dark'] { --nova-tint-accent: rgb(169 155 255 / 0.18); }
```

## Contrast

Built-in colour pairs are checked against WCAG AA in both themes on every build. If you add colours, check them with `contrastRatio` from `@omni/core`.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/features/utilities.md ====

# Utilities

Helpers exported from `@omni/core` for logic your app shares with the components.

| Area | Functions | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dialogs | `confirm`, `prompt` | Promise-based dialogs ([Overlays](overlays.md)) |
| Notifications | `toast`, `toast.success`, `.error`, `.warning`, `.info`, `.dismiss` | Toast messages |
| HTML | `sanitizeHTML`, `isSafeLink`, `isSafeImage` | Safe display ([Safe HTML](safe-html.md)) |
| Files | `validateFiles`, `acceptsType`, `formatBytes` | Upload rules ([File upload](file-upload.md)) |
| Export | `toCSV`, `escapeCell`, `safeFilename` | CSV with formula-injection guard |
| Dates | `parseISO`, `toISO`, `addDays`, `addMonths`, `monthGrid`, `clampISO` | Calendar maths ([Dates](dates.md)) |
| Times | `parseTime`, `toMinutes`, `durationMinutes`, `timeSlots`, `inTimeRange` | Time maths |
| Ranges | `normaliseRange`, `pickDay`, `inRange`, `rangeLength`, `presetRanges` | Date ranges |
| Colour | `hexToHsv`, `hsvToHex`, `contrastRatio`, `luminance`, `readableOn`, `mix` | Colour maths |
| Theme | `generateTheme`, `themeToCSS`, `setThemeMode`, `getThemeMode`, `onThemeChange` | Palettes and modes |
| Charts | `linearScale`, `niceTicks`, `extent`, `compact`, `bars`, `donutSlices` | Chart maths |
| Lists | `moveItem`, `keyboardMove`, `dropIndex`, `moveCard` | Reordering |
| Calendar | `eventsOnDay`, `layoutTimed`, `weekDays` | Scheduler maths |
| Virtualising | `virtualRange`, `scrollToRow` | Large lists |
| Motion | `animateIn`, `staggerIn`, `playExit`, `withViewTransition`, `prefersReducedMotion` | Animations |
| Presence | `nextPhase`, `isMounted` | Exit animation state |
| Messages | `setMessages`, `resetMessages`, `t`, `DEFAULT_MESSAGES` | Translation ([i18n](i18n.md)) |

Full signatures are in the [component and API reference](../../../packages/core/dist-docs/API.md) and in the TypeScript types shipped with each package.
