==== SOURCE: docs/users/frameworks/angular.md ====

# Angular

Works with Angular 17 and later, using standalone components. Each Nova component is a standalone Angular component with inputs, outputs and forms integration.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @omni/core @omni/css @omni/angular
```

Add the stylesheet to `angular.json`:

```json
"styles": ["node_modules/@omni/css/dist/nova.min.css", "src/styles.css"]
```

## Use components

```ts
import { Component, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { UiButton, UiInput, UiCard, ThemeService, toast, confirm } from '@omni/angular';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-profile',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [UiButton, UiInput, UiCard],
  template: `
    <ui-card variant="raised">
      <ui-input label="Email" [value]="email()" (uiInput)="email.set($event.detail)"></ui-input>
      <ui-button (click)="save()">Save</ui-button>
    </ui-card>
  `,
})
export class ProfileComponent {
  readonly theme = inject(ThemeService);
  readonly email = signal('');
  save() { toast.success('Saved'); }
}
```

## Forms

The form controls provide Angular value accessors, so `ngModel` and reactive forms work:

```html
<ui-input name="email" label="Email" [(ngModel)]="email" required></ui-input>
<ui-select name="owner" [(ngModel)]="owner" [options]="owners"></ui-select>
```

Use `[(ngModel)]` for two-way binding, or `[formControl]` with `ReactiveFormsModule`. The value accessors are generated from the component configuration in `stencil.config.ts`.

## Outputs

Events are outputs in the `ui*` form: `(uiChange)`, `(uiInput)`, `(uiSearch)`. The payload is in `$event.detail`.

## Theme service

`ThemeService` exposes `mode` and `resolved` as signals and `set(mode)` to change them.

## Exit animations

Angular has no built-in exit animation for removed content. Call `playExit(element)` from `@omni/angular` before you remove an element, or use the `phase` approach from [Motion](../features/motion.md).

## The rich text editor

```ts
import { UiEditor } from '@omni/angular/editor';
```

## Gotchas

- **`ui-*` elements not known**: import the standalone component, or add `CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA` only as a last resort.
- **Entry-point build**: the editor is a secondary entry point, so import it from `@omni/angular/editor`.
- **Playground**: `apps/playground-angular` shows a working setup. It has not yet been built in CI; see [Testing](../../humans/testing.md).


==== SOURCE: docs/users/frameworks/css-only.md ====

# CSS-only usage

Use `@omni/css` alone for static pages, server-rendered templates or email-to-web layouts where no JavaScript runs. You get layout, typography, utilities and CSS-only components (buttons, cards, badges, alerts, form fields, tables).

## Install and load

```bash
pnpm add @omni/css
```

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@omni/css/dist/nova.min.css" />
<body class="nova-base">
  <main class="nova-container nova-section nova-stack">
    <h1 class="nova-h2">Pricing</h1>
    <div class="nova-grid-auto nova-grid-auto-md nova-gap-4">
      <article class="nova-card nova-card-raised">
        <div class="nova-card__body nova-stack nova-stack-sm">
          <h2 class="nova-h5">Team</h2>
          <button class="nova-btn">Choose</button>
        </div>
      </article>
    </div>
  </main>
</body>
```

## What you get

- Layout primitives: `nova-container`, `nova-page`, `nova-stack`, `nova-cluster`, `nova-grid-auto`, `nova-sidebar`, `nova-switcher`, `nova-shell`.
- Responsive utilities: `nova-md-cols-3`, `nova-hide-below-md`, `nova-md-px-8`.
- Container queries: `nova-cq` with `nova-cq-md-cols-2`.
- CSS-only components with the same look as the web components.
- Scroll-linked motion: `nova-scroll-reveal`, `nova-scroll-progress`.

The full guide, with breakpoints, recipes and accessibility notes, is in [packages/css/GUIDELINES.md](../../../packages/css/GUIDELINES.md). A live, resizable version is in `packages/css/docs/index.html`.

## Limits

CSS-only components can't open menus, validate forms or fetch data. When you need behaviour, use the web components instead; they match these visually.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/frameworks/nextjs.md ====

# Next.js (App Router)

Nova works with the App Router and the Pages Router. Components are client components, so they run in the browser; the layout and the theme script run on the server.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @omni/core @omni/css @omni/react
```

## Root layout: stylesheet, theme script, no flash

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import '@omni/css/nova.css';
import { themeInitScript } from '@omni/react/server';

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    // suppressHydrationWarning: the script sets data-theme before React hydrates.
    <html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning>
      <head>
        <script dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: themeInitScript }} />
      </head>
      <body className="nova-base">{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

For a safe viewport on phones add it to `app/layout.tsx`:

```tsx
export const viewport = { width: 'device-width', initialScale: 1, viewportFit: 'cover' };
```

## Using components

Mark any file that uses Nova components as a client component:

```tsx
'use client';

import { UiButton, UiCard, useTheme } from '@omni/react';

export default function Page() {
  const { mode, resolved } = useTheme();
  return <UiCard><UiButton>Save</UiButton></UiCard>;
}
```

Components can be imported from server files, because the package is marked `"use client"` in its build. Hooks (`useTheme`, `usePresence`) and event handlers still need a client component.

## Editor in Next.js

```tsx
'use client';
import dynamic from 'next/dynamic';
const UiEditor = dynamic(() => import('@omni/react/editor').then((m) => m.UiEditor), { ssr: false });
```

Loading the editor with `ssr: false` keeps Tiptap out of the server bundle.

## Gotchas

- **Hydration mismatch on theme**: keep `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>` and the theme script in `<head>`.
- **Charts and tables on the server**: they render their markup, but measurements (sizes, scroll) happen in the browser. Keep layout dependent on CSS, not on JavaScript measurement, when you can.
- **Server rendering of components is not yet provided by the package.** Components render their shell on the client. Stencil's hydration output is planned; until it lands, use the client-component pattern above.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/frameworks/react.md ====

# React

Works with React 18 and 19. Components are wrapped so props and events look like normal React.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @omni/core @omni/css @omni/react
```

Import the stylesheet in your entry file, once:

```tsx
// src/main.tsx
import '@omni/css/nova.css';
import { App } from './App';
```

## Use components

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { UiButton, UiInput, UiSelect, UiCard, toast } from '@omni/react';

export function Profile() {
  const [owner, setOwner] = useState('');
  return (
    <UiCard variant="raised">
      <UiInput label="Email" name="email" type="email" required />
      <UiSelect
        label="Owner"
        searchable
        value={owner}
        options={[{ value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Lovelace' }, { value: 'grace', label: 'Grace Hopper' }]}
        onUiChange={(e) => setOwner(String(e.detail))}
      />
      <UiButton onClick={() => toast.success('Saved')}>Save</UiButton>
    </UiCard>
  );
}
```

Events are `onUi<Name>` with the payload in `e.detail`. Props that take objects (`options`, `columns`, `rows`, `series`) are plain JavaScript values.

## Forms

Give each control a `name` inside a `<form>`, then read the values from `FormData`:

```tsx
<form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); const data = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(e.currentTarget)); }}>
  <UiInput name="email" label="Email" required />
  <UiButton type="submit">Send</UiButton>
</form>
```

Controls with values also accept `value` and `onUiChange` if you prefer controlled state.

## Hooks and helpers

| Export | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `useTheme()` | Current mode and resolved theme, plus `setMode` |
| `usePresence(open, ms)` | Keep an element mounted while it animates out |
| `toast`, `confirm`, `prompt` | Notifications and dialogs |
| `generateTheme`, `themeToCSS` | Build a brand palette |
| `contrastRatio`, `niceTicks`, `compact` | Utilities used by charts and theming |

## Exit animations

```tsx
import { usePresence, UiCard } from '@omni/react';

const { mounted, phase } = usePresence(open, 180);
{mounted && <UiCard className={phase === 'exiting' ? 'fade-out' : 'fade-in'}>…</UiCard>}
```

`ms` must match your CSS exit animation. Users who prefer reduced motion are removed immediately.

## The rich text editor

```tsx
import { UiEditor } from '@omni/react/editor';
```

It's a separate entry point, so it only loads where you import it. See [Rich text editor](../features/editor.md).

## Page blocks

```tsx
import { LoginBlock, PricingBlock, DashboardBlock, SettingsBlock, OnboardingBlock } from '@omni/react';
```

Copy and adapt them. See [Page blocks](../features/page-blocks.md).

## Gotchas

- **Event names**: use `onUiChange`, not `onChange`. The native `onChange` still works on native inputs.
- **Server rendering**: components render on the client. Use `'use client'` in Next.js (see [Next.js](nextjs.md)).
- **Refs**: call methods through the element ref, for example `ref.current.focusInput()`.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/frameworks/tailwind.md ====

# Tailwind CSS preset

The preset adds Nova colours, radii, shadows, fonts, durations and z-indexes to Tailwind. Each one is a CSS variable, so your Tailwind classes follow light, dark and brand themes automatically.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add -D @omni/tailwind tailwindcss
```

## Configure

```js
// tailwind.config.js
module.exports = {
  presets: [require('@omni/tailwind')],
  content: ['./src/**/*.{html,tsx,vue,ts}'],
};
```

Import the Nova stylesheet too, so the variables exist:

```css
@import '@omni/css/nova.css';
@tailwind base;
@tailwind components;
@tailwind utilities;
```

## Classes

| Utility | Resolves to |
| --- | --- |
| `bg-nova-surface`, `bg-nova-sunken`, `bg-nova-raised` | Surface tokens |
| `text-nova-fg`, `text-nova-muted`, `text-nova-subtle` | Text tokens |
| `bg-nova-accent`, `text-nova-on-accent`, `bg-nova-accent-soft` | Accent tokens |
| `border-nova-border`, `border-nova-border-strong` | Border tokens |
| `text-nova-danger`, `bg-nova-success` and so on | Status colours |
| `rounded-nova-control`, `rounded-nova-surface`, `rounded-nova-pill` | Radius tokens |
| `shadow-nova-sm`, `shadow-nova-md`, `shadow-nova-lg` | Shadows |
| `font-nova-sans`, `font-nova-mono` | Font stacks |
| `duration-nova-fast`, `duration-nova-base` | Motion timings |
| `z-nova-dropdown`, `z-nova-modal`, `z-nova-toast` | Layers |

## Mixing with components

Nova web components keep their own styling inside their shadow root, so Tailwind classes apply to the elements around them, not inside. Use Tailwind for page layout and Nova components for controls.

## Dark mode

Set `darkMode` as you like, or leave Tailwind's default. Nova's tokens already switch with `data-theme`, so you don't need `dark:` variants for Nova colours.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/frameworks/vanilla.md ====

# Plain HTML and web components

Use this when you're not using a framework, or when you want to use Nova in any framework that can render HTML.

## Install and load

```bash
pnpm add @omni/core @omni/css
```

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover" />
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@omni/css/dist/nova.min.css" />
    <script type="module">
      import { defineCustomElements } from '/node_modules/@omni/core/loader/index.js';
      defineCustomElements();
    </script>
  </head>
  <body class="nova-base">
    <ui-button variant="primary">Save</ui-button>
    <ui-input label="Email" type="email" name="email" required></ui-input>
  </body>
</html>
```

Bundlers resolve these paths for you. In a bundled app, write `import '@omni/css/nova.css'` and `import { defineCustomElements } from '@omni/core/loader'`.

## Setting objects and arrays

Attributes are strings. Set complex values as properties:

```html
<ui-select id="owner" label="Owner" searchable></ui-select>
<script type="module">
  const el = document.getElementById('owner');
  el.options = [{ value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Lovelace' }, { value: 'grace', label: 'Grace Hopper' }];
  el.addEventListener('ui-change', (e) => console.log('chosen', e.detail));
</script>
```

## Methods

Call methods directly on the element: `await el.focusInput()`, `await editor.getContentHTML()`, `await table.exportCSV()`.

## Slots

```html
<ui-button>
  <ui-icon slot="start" name="check"></ui-icon>
  Save
</ui-button>
```

## Next steps

[Concepts](../concepts.md) · [Feature guides](../features/README.md) · [Component reference](../../../packages/core/dist-docs/API.md)


==== SOURCE: docs/users/frameworks/vite.md ====

# Vite

Vite works with React, Vue, Angular or plain JavaScript. Use the framework guide for the component layer, and this page for the build.

## Create a project

```bash
pnpm create vite my-app --template react-ts   # or vue-ts, vanilla-ts
cd my-app
pnpm add @omni/core @omni/css @omni/react
```

## Entry file

```tsx
// src/main.tsx
import '@omni/css/nova.css';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { App } from './App';

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(<App />);
```

Vue and plain JavaScript work the same way: import the stylesheet first, then mount the app.

## Dark mode before first paint

Add the theme script to `index.html` before your scripts:

```html
<script>
  document.documentElement.dataset.theme =
    localStorage.getItem('nova-ui-theme') ||
    (matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches ? 'dark' : 'light');
</script>
```

## Splitting the editor

The rich text editor is large. Import it from its own entry point so Vite puts it in a separate chunk:

```tsx
const { UiEditor } = await import('@omni/react/editor');
```

## Workspace development

If you're developing Nova and an app together in one monorepo, depend on the packages with `workspace:*` so changes appear without publishing.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/frameworks/vue.md ====

# Vue 3

Vue wrappers are generated from the same component manifest as the other frameworks. They're thin: props go in, events come out as Vue emits.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @omni/core @omni/css @omni/vue
```

## Setup

```ts
// src/main.ts
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import '@omni/css/nova.css';
import { defineCustomElements } from '@omni/core/loader';
import App from './App.vue';

defineCustomElements();
createApp(App).mount('#app');
```

## Use components

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';
import { UiButton, UiInput, UiSelect } from '@omni/vue';

const owner = ref('');
const owners = [{ value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Lovelace' }, { value: 'grace', label: 'Grace Hopper' }];
</script>

<template>
  <UiInput label="Email" name="email" type="email" required />
  <UiSelect label="Owner" :options="owners" searchable @ui-change="(e) => (owner = e.detail)" />
  <UiButton>Save</UiButton>
</template>
```

- Props use Vue's camelCase names: `:options="owners"`, `:page-size` and `pageSize` both work.
- Events are listened to with `@ui-change` (Vue maps it to the emitted `uiChange`).
- Slots work as normal Vue slots.

## Forms

Use `:value` with `@ui-change` to keep a control in sync with your state. Plain `v-model` isn't wired for these components yet, so don't rely on it.

## Generated wrappers

The wrappers live in `packages/vue/src/components.ts` and are regenerated with `pnpm docs`. Don't edit that file; change the component source and regenerate.

## Gotchas

- **Components not registered**: call `defineCustomElements()` once before mounting.
- **Object props**: they're passed as properties, so a plain array works.
- **Status**: the generated wrappers parse and cover all components, but they have not been run against Vue in CI yet. Report any issue you hit.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/getting-started.md ====

# Getting started

Nova UI is a design system with one set of components that works in plain HTML, React, Next.js, Vite, Angular and Vue, plus a CSS library and a Tailwind preset. This page gets you to a working screen in about five minutes. Pick your framework afterwards in [Frameworks](frameworks/README.md).

## 1. Install

Choose what you need. Most apps need only the first line.

```bash
pnpm add @omni/core            # web components, tokens, theme, utilities
pnpm add @omni/css             # layout classes, utilities, CSS-only components (optional)
pnpm add @omni/react           # React wrappers (React, Next.js, Vite + React)
pnpm add @omni/angular         # Angular standalone wrappers
pnpm add @omni/vue             # Vue 3 wrappers
pnpm add @omni/editor          # rich text editor (optional, heavy, built on Tiptap)
pnpm add -D @omni/tailwind     # Tailwind preset (optional)
```

## 2. Add the stylesheet

Import one stylesheet once, near the top of your app. It contains the design tokens, the reset, layout classes and utilities.

```css
@import '@omni/css/nova.css';
```

Also set the viewport so the layout respects phone notches and users can still zoom:

```html
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover" />
```

Never add `user-scalable=no` or `maximum-scale=1`. It blocks zoom and fails WCAG.

If you want Google's Material Symbols instead of the built-in icons, add the font link from [Icons](features/icons.md) to your page's `<head>`. Skip it otherwise.

## 3. Use a component

Every framework uses the same component names and the same props. Only the syntax changes.

| Framework | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| HTML | `<ui-button variant="primary">Save</ui-button>` |
| React | `<UiButton variant="primary">Save</UiButton>` |
| Angular | `<ui-button variant="primary">Save</ui-button>` (standalone import `UiButton`) |
| Vue | `<UiButton variant="primary">Save</UiButton>` (from `@omni/vue`) |

## 4. Respond to events

Events are named after the component and the action, prefixed with `ui`. In HTML they are DOM events; in React and Angular they're the same events in each framework's syntax.

| Framework | Listen to `uiChange` |
| --- | --- |
| HTML | `el.addEventListener('ui-change', (e) => e.detail)` |
| React | `<UiSelect onUiChange={(e) => e.detail} />` |
| Angular | `<ui-select (uiChange)="onChange($event.detail)" />` |
| Vue | `<UiSelect @ui-change="onChange" />` |

The `detail` carries the new value. Each component's reference lists its events and their payloads.

## 5. Turn on theming

Nova follows the operating-system light or dark setting by default. To let users choose, call `setThemeMode('light' | 'dark' | 'system')`, or drop in `<ui-theme-toggle>`. The choice is remembered. See [Theming](features/theming.md).

## 6. Where to go next

- [Releases](releases.md): what to install, how versions work, how to upgrade and roll back.

- [Concepts](concepts.md): how the pieces fit together, and the few rules that matter.
- [Your framework](frameworks/README.md): setup and gotchas for your stack.
- [Feature guides](features/README.md): forms, overlays, navigation, tables, charts, editor and more.
- [Component reference](../../packages/core/dist-docs/API.md): every component, prop, event, method and slot.
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md): when something doesn't render.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/releases.md ====

# Release guide: installing and upgrading Nova UI

For developers using Nova UI in their own apps. It covers what you install, how versions work, how to upgrade safely, and how to check a release.

Maintainers who publish releases should read [docs/humans/release-manual.md](../humans/release-manual.md) instead.

## Contents

1. [What you install](#1-what-you-install)
2. [Versions](#2-versions)
3. [Installing](#3-installing)
4. [Peer dependencies](#4-peer-dependencies)
5. [Upgrading](#5-upgrading)
6. [Reading a changelog](#6-reading-a-changelog)
7. [Pre-releases](#7-pre-releases)
8. [Pinning and rolling back](#8-pinning-and-rolling-back)
9. [Checking a release](#9-checking-a-release)
10. [Browser and runtime support](#10-browser-and-runtime-support)
11. [Deprecations](#11-deprecations)
12. [Troubleshooting](#12-troubleshooting)

## 1. What you install

Nova UI is published as seven npm packages. You install only the ones you use.

| Package | Install it when | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@omni/core` | Always: the web components, tokens, theme and utilities | Nothing |
| `@omni/css` | You want layout classes, utilities or CSS-only components | Nothing |
| `@omni/react` | Your app uses React, Next.js or Vite with React | `react`, `react-dom` |
| `@omni/angular` | Your app uses Angular | `@angular/core`, `@angular/common` |
| `@omni/vue` | Your app uses Vue 3 | `vue` |
| `@omni/editor` | You want the rich text editor | Nothing extra (it uses `@omni/core`) |
| `@omni/tailwind` | You use Tailwind CSS and want Nova colours and radii as classes | `tailwindcss` |

A typical React app installs `core`, `css` and `react`. An Angular app installs `core`, `css` and `angular`.

## 2. Versions

All seven packages are released together, at the same version, so `@omni/react@0.3.0` works with `@omni/core@0.3.0`. Keep them on the same version.

Nova is pre-1.0. The version number means:

- **Patch** (`0.3.1`): bug fixes. Safe to take without reading anything else.
- **Minor** (`0.3.0`): new components, props, events or tokens. Existing code keeps working, but read the changelog.
- **Major** (`1.0.0`, later): removals or renames. Each one comes with a migration note.

Before 1.0, a minor release may still change a prop or event. The changelog says so when it happens.

## 3. Installing

Install the packages for your framework, at the same version:

```bash
# React, Next.js or Vite with React
npm install @omni/core @omni/css @omni/react

# Angular
npm install @omni/core @omni/css @omni/angular

# Vue 3
npm install @omni/core @omni/css @omni/vue

# Add the rich text editor (optional)
npm install @omni/editor

# Add Tailwind preset (optional)
npm install -D @omni/tailwind
```

pnpm and yarn work the same way: use `pnpm add` or `yarn add` with the same package names.

Then import the stylesheet once, in your entry file:

```js
import '@omni/css/nova.css';
```

See [Getting started](getting-started.md) for the first component.

## 4. Peer dependencies

Some packages expect you to install a framework yourself. npm 7 and later installs peer dependencies automatically, and shows a warning if the versions don't match.

| Package | Peer | Version range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@omni/react` | `react`, `react-dom` | `>=18` |
| `@omni/angular` | `@angular/core`, `@angular/common` | `>=17` |
| `@omni/vue` | `vue` | `>=3.3.0` |
| `@omni/tailwind` | `tailwindcss` | `>=3.3.0` |
| `@omni/react`, `@omni/angular` | `@omni/editor` | optional: only if you use the editor entry point |
| `@omni/editor`, `@omni/vue` | `@omni/core` | `^0.1.0` (the same minor as your other Nova packages) |

If npm reports a peer conflict, install the framework version in the range above, or upgrade the Nova packages together.

## 5. Upgrading

Upgrade every Nova package together:

```bash
npm install @omni/core@latest @omni/css@latest @omni/react@latest
```

Then, in this order:

1. **Read the changelog** for every version between yours and the new one (section 6).
2. **Upgrade in a branch**, and run your tests and a visual check of the screens you use.
3. **Look for deprecation warnings** in the browser console (section 11).
4. **Check the migration notes** for any breaking change you hit.
5. **Ship** once your screens look right.

To see what would change before installing:

```bash
npm outdated @omni/core @omni/css @omni/react
```

To see every version that exists:

```bash
npm view @omni/core versions --json
```

## 6. Reading a changelog

Each package has a `CHANGELOG.md`, on npm (`npm view @omni/core` shows the repository link) and in the GitHub release for each version. Every entry is one of:

- **Major changes**: removed or renamed APIs. Read these first.
- **Minor changes**: new features.
- **Patch changes**: fixes.

A changeset-style entry looks like this:

> **Breaking:** `ui-table` no longer sorts server data by default. Set `manual` and handle `ui-query-change`.

Each breaking change lists what to do instead. If an entry doesn't say, open an issue and ask.

The [component reference](../../packages/core/dist-docs/API.md) describes the current API, so after an upgrade, check the parts of it you use.

## 7. Pre-releases

Release candidates are published under the `next` tag, so the default install keeps getting the latest stable version:

```bash
npm install @omni/core@next @omni/css@next @omni/react@next
```

Pre-releases can change between releases. Use them to test an upcoming version, not in production.

To go back to stable:

```bash
npm install @omni/core@latest @omni/css@latest @omni/react@latest
```

## 8. Pinning and rolling back

To stop upgrades from happening automatically, pin the exact version in `package.json`:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@omni/core": "0.3.0",
  "@omni/react": "0.3.0"
}
```

Without the `^`, npm will not move to a newer version when you run `npm install`.

To roll back after a bad upgrade, install the previous version of every Nova package:

```bash
npm install @omni/core@0.2.0 @omni/css@0.2.0 @omni/react@0.2.0
```

Then check the lockfile (`package-lock.json`) is committed, so the rolled-back versions are what everyone on the team gets.

## 9. Checking a release

Every release is built and checked before it is published, but you can verify your copy:

**Version and source.** The package page on npm shows the version, the repository and, for releases built by GitHub Actions, "Built and signed on GitHub Actions" with a link to the workflow run. That run is the exact build you installed.

**Checksums.** Each GitHub release attaches the packed tarballs and a `SHA256SUMS.txt`. To check a download:

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt
```

It prints `OK` for each file that matches.

**Installed files.** The package contains only the built output, not source:

```bash
npm pack @omni/angular@0.3.0 --dry-run
```

You should see `dist/` files and `package.json`, not `src/`.

## 10. Browser and runtime support

Nova targets current evergreen browsers (the latest versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, and the mobile browsers of the same period). Older browsers may work, but are not tested.

Some features depend on newer browser support, and degrade where it is missing:

| Feature | Needs | Without it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cascade layers (`@layer`) | Browsers from 2022 | Use `nova.compat.css`, which has no layers |
| Container queries (`nova-cq-*`) | Browsers from 2023 | Design the narrow layout as the default |
| View Transitions | Chrome, Edge, Safari 18+ | Updates happen without the transition |
| Scroll-linked motion (`nova-scroll-reveal`) | Browsers that support scroll timelines (`animation-timeline`) | Content shows without the animation |
| Popover (menus, tooltips) | Current browsers | Floating panels fall back to positioned elements |

Reduced-motion and high-contrast preferences are respected.

## 11. Deprecations

Before 1.0, a removal or rename can happen in a minor release, and the changelog says so under Major changes, with the replacement. Nova does not yet print deprecation warnings in the browser console, so check the changelog after each upgrade.

Once Nova reaches 1.0, APIs will be deprecated in one release and removed no earlier than the next major release, with a warning in the console in between.

## 12. Troubleshooting

**`npm ERR! peer dep conflict`.** A peer dependency is outside the range in section 4. Install the framework version the message asks for, or upgrade the Nova packages together.

**Components render as unstyled or not at all.** The stylesheet is missing. Import `@omni/css/nova.css` once in your entry file (section 3).

**`@omni/core` versions don't match.** Two Nova packages are on different versions. Install all of them at the same version, then delete `node_modules` and the lockfile only if the install still fails.

**Icons show as empty squares.** You switched to the Material icon set without loading its font. Load the font, or use the Nova set. See [Icons](features/icons.md).

**After upgrading, a prop or event stopped working.** Check the changelog for that version under Major or Minor changes. The migration note tells you the new name.

**Still stuck.** Open an issue at the repository with the package versions (`npm ls @omni/core @omni/css @omni/react`), your framework version and a minimal reproduction.


==== SOURCE: docs/users/troubleshooting.md ====

# Troubleshooting

Symptom, likely cause, fix. If your problem isn't here, check the browser console first: most problems log a clear message.

## The component renders as plain text or an empty box

- **Stylesheet not imported.** Add `@import '@omni/css/nova.css';` once in your app.
- **Component not registered.** In plain HTML, call `defineCustomElements()` from `@omni/core/loader`. In React and Angular the wrappers register components when imported; if you see `not defined`, import the loader once in your entry file.
- **Wrong tag name.** Tags are `ui-` followed by the kebab-case name: `ui-date-picker`, not `ui-datepicker`.

## "`<ui-toaster>` is not registered" when calling `toast()`

Render `<UiToaster />` (or `<ui-toaster>`) once near the root of your app. `toast()` creates one automatically in most cases, but the warning means it wasn't ready. Check that the component is imported.

## Dark mode flashes on page load

Add the theme script before your stylesheet in `<head>`. In Next.js use `themeInitScript` from `@omni/react/server` in the root layout (see [Next.js](frameworks/nextjs.md)).

## Form values are missing on submit

- Give the control a `name`.
- Make sure the control is inside a `<form>`.
- For React, read values with `new FormData(event.currentTarget)` or from your own state via `onUiChange`.

## Angular form binding does nothing

Use `ngModel` or `formControl` with the Nova form controls. They provide value accessors automatically. If you bind with `[value]` and `(uiChange)`, update your model in the handler.

## Table rows are not sorted or filtered in server mode

Set `manual` and handle `uiQueryChange`. In manual mode the table shows the rows you pass; it does not sort or filter them.

## Table is slow with thousands of rows

Enable `virtual` with a `maxHeight` and a fixed `rowHeight`. Turn off `paginate` for a single long scrollable list. See [Data tables](features/data-tables.md).

## Chart shows no data

The `series` values must be numbers. Strings like `"12"` are ignored. Check that `labels` has one entry per value.

## Editor content is lost or unsafe

The editor's value is HTML. Store it as HTML, sanitise it before rendering it anywhere else, and load it back with `setContent()` or the `value` prop. Uploads need an `uploadHandler`; without one, images are embedded as data URLs and attachments are refused.

## Focus ring is missing or doubled

Focus rings are drawn by the component. Don't add your own `outline: none` to Nova elements. If a focusable element you built yourself shows a double ring, add `class="hydrated"` only to Nova components; the reset leaves custom elements alone.

## Text is not translated

Call `setMessages()` before the first render, and use keys from `DEFAULT_MESSAGES` (exported from `@omni/core`).

## Tailwind classes have no effect

Add the preset to `tailwind.config.js` and include the Nova paths in `content` if you use components with Tailwind classes. Classes such as `bg-nova-accent` need the preset loaded.

## Something still broken

1. Note the component tag, framework and version.
2. Copy the minimal code that reproduces it.
3. Open an issue with those three items. Maintainers can use the test harness in [Testing](../humans/testing.md) to reproduce it.


==== SOURCE: docs/humans/architecture.md ====

# Architecture

For maintainers and contributors. Read this before changing the packages.

## Packages

```
packages/
  core/      @omni/core     Stencil web components (71 in core), tokens, theme, utilities, i18n, docs generator
  editor/    @omni/editor   rich text editor (Tiptap), separate so Tiptap isn't a core dependency
  react/     @omni/react    generated React wrappers + hooks + page blocks; /editor and /server entry points
  angular/   @omni/angular  generated standalone proxies + ThemeService; /editor secondary entry point
  vue/       @omni/vue      Vue 3 wrappers generated from the manifest (scripts/generate.mjs)
  css/       @omni/css      layout, utilities, CSS-only components, print, guidelines; framework-free
  tailwind/  @omni/tailwind Tailwind preset mapping utilities to --nova-* tokens
apps/
  playground-vite/   React + Vite demo of every feature
  playground-next/   Next.js App Router demo
  playground-angular/ Angular standalone demo
docs/                user, human and agent documentation (this folder)
```

## Layers

1. **Tokens** (`core/src/global/tokens.css`, `css/src/tokens.css`). Colours, type, space, radius, shadow, motion, layout sizes, all as `--nova-*` custom properties. Single source of truth for every framework.
2. **Pure logic** (`core/src/utils/*.ts`, `core/src/i18n`, `editor/src/.../uploads.ts`). No DOM and no framework. Every rule that matters lives here so it can be tested in Node.
3. **Components** (`core/src/components/*`). Stencil web components. Each has a `.tsx` and a `.css`. Components use the logic layer and tokens; they don't hard-code colours or strings.
4. **Wrappers**. Generated for React, Angular and Vue from the component metadata. Hand-written only for hooks, helpers and blocks.
5. **Layout and utilities** (`css`). Independent of the web components. Usable on their own.

## Generated code: do not edit

| File | Generated by | Regenerate with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/react/src/components/stencil-generated/*` | `@stencil/react-output-target` | `pnpm build` |
| `packages/angular/src/lib/stencil-generated/*` | `@stencil/angular-output-target` | `pnpm build` |
| `packages/css/src/generated/utilities.css` | `scripts/generate-utilities.mjs` | `pnpm --filter @omni/css generate` |
| `packages/core/dist-docs/*` | `scripts/generate-docs.mjs` | `pnpm docs` |
| `packages/vue/src/components.ts` | `scripts/generate.mjs` | `pnpm docs` |
| `docs/llms-full.txt` | `scripts/build-llms.mjs` | `pnpm docs:agents` |

Change the source, then regenerate. CI fails if a generated file is out of date.

## Key design decisions

- **Web components, not framework components.** One implementation runs everywhere. The cost is that frameworks must map props and events, which the generators do.
- **Native elements where possible.** Dialogs use `<dialog>`; popovers use the Popover API (top layer, no clipping); forms use `ElementInternals` so controls submit natively.
- **Light DOM for the editor.** ProseMirror's selection, IME and spellcheck behave best outside a shadow root. The editor's CSS is prefixed so it can't leak.
- **No runtime animation library.** Motion uses the Web Animations API, CSS transitions and the scroll timeline. Everything respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Contrast is a build check.** Token pairs are measured against WCAG AA in both themes. The generator enforces the same rule for brand palettes.
- **Props never shadow DOM members.** `scripts/check-prop-names.mjs` checks all `@Prop` and `@Method` names against `HTMLElement`. (`Element.prefix` and `Element.getHTML` already caused bugs.)
- **Event names are `ui`-prefixed and kebab-cased in the DOM** (`ui-change`), camel-cased in frameworks (`uiChange`).

## Data flow for a value

User input → component updates its own state → emits `uiChange` with `detail` → framework wrapper forwards it as `onUiChange` (React), `(uiChange)` (Angular), or `@ui-change` (Vue). Form controls also call `setFormValue` on their `ElementInternals`, so native forms see the value without any code.

## Where things live

| Need | Look in |
| --- | --- |
| A component's behaviour | `packages/core/src/components/<name>/<name>.tsx` |
| Its styling | `packages/core/src/components/<name>/<name>.css` |
| The rules it uses | `packages/core/src/utils/<topic>.ts` |
| Its strings | `packages/core/src/i18n/messages.ts` |
| Its tests | `packages/core/test/<topic>.test.mjs` |
| Its docs | `docs/users/features/<area>.md` and the generated API reference |


==== SOURCE: docs/humans/status.md ====

# Project status

An honest picture of what is built, what is tested, and what has only been written. Update this with every release.

## Built

| Area | Components or features | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Foundation | Tokens, light, dark and system themes, theme toggle, icons (68), i18n catalogue (94 keys), motion helpers | Logic tests, CSS checks |
| Forms | Input, textarea, checkbox, switch, radio group, slider, rating, OTP, tags, field wrapper, date, date range, time, colour, calendar | Logic tests (date, range, time, colour); type-check |
| Overlays | Modal, drawer, popover, tooltip, dropdown, context menu, searchable select, command palette, toaster, confirm and prompt | Queue and focus logic tests; type-check |
| Navigation | Tabs, accordion, breadcrumb, pagination, stepper, nav menu, menubar, sidebar, split panes, collapse | Type-check; keyboard logic partly tested |
| Data | Table (sort, search, select, paginate, export, resize, expand, virtual), tree, virtual list, sortable, kanban, scheduler | Layout, export, window, reorder, calendar logic tests; type-check |
| Charts | Line, area, bar, donut, sparkline | Chart maths tests (13); type-check |
| Files | File upload with validation | Validation tests (7); type-check |
| Content | Safe HTML, rich text editor, page blocks | Sanitiser security tests (11 in a real DOM); editor helper tests; type-check |
| Layout and CSS | Layout primitives, utilities, container queries, CSS components, print, scroll-linked motion | Build checks, 46 contrast pairs, 2-build browser layout tests |
| Ecosystem | React, Angular, Vue wrappers, Tailwind preset, generated API docs, editor autocomplete data, CI workflow | Generated and parsed or type-checked; Tailwind tokens tested |
| Documentation | Human, user and agent docs for every feature and framework; `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `AGENTS.md` | `pnpm docs:check`: every component documented, every prop and event named in the guides exists, every link resolves |

## Not yet verified

- **A real `pnpm install && pnpm build`.** The sandbox used to write this code couldn't reach the package registry, so Stencil has never compiled these components. This is the single biggest open risk.
- **Component behaviour in browsers**, beyond the CSS layer.
- **Frameworks running the wrappers** (React, Angular, Vue) end to end.
- **Accessibility with screen readers and Windows High Contrast.**
- **Server rendering.** Components render on the client. Stencil's hydration output is not enabled.
- **Stencil spec tests and CI runs.** The CI workflow is written but has not executed.

## Documentation limits

- The guides describe intended behaviour from the source. Examples have been checked for prop and event names, not run in a browser.
- Framework guides for Angular and Vue describe setups that aren't built in CI yet.

## Known gaps

- Drag-and-drop announcements for screen readers.
- Editor suggestion popup is not announced as a linked combobox.
- Table virtual mode and expansion don't combine.
- Icons are hand-drawn, not imported from a licensed set; check each visually.
- Angular playground has not been built.

## Next

1. Run the real build and fix what it reports.
2. Enable Stencil hydration for server rendering.
3. Add Stencil spec tests for interaction behaviour.
4. Run the wrappers inside each framework in CI.
